title: A store an operator configured is authorized by the configuring, and may be a Unix socket
scope:
what authorizes an outbound connection to a store named in root-owned configuration, and
how such a store is reached over a Unix domain socket. Covers the grant `Core\Cache::shared()` and
`Core\RateLimit::consume` ask, the spelling a socket takes in `[cache.shared] url` and in
`[db.<name>] host`, what a platform without `AF_UNIX` does with one, and how a Postgres socket path
is read. Not in scope: the address policy itself, which is [0058](0058.md)
§ 3's and is only *narrowed in reach* here; the two tiers and why the local one is a cache rather
than a store, which is [0059](0059.md) § 1's; the transport, which
`crates/nvs-host/src/net.rs` owns and already carries.
dependsOnText:
[0058](0058.md), whose § 3 already decided that an endpoint
an operator wrote is not attacker-influenceable, and [0059](0059.md),
which decides there is a coherent tier to reach at all.

summary.headline: A configured store is already authorized, and may be a Unix socket
summary.body:
When an operator writes a cache or database endpoint into root-owned configuration, that act is
the authorization. A program asking for the shared cache or a rate limiter asks for the
`cache.shared` grant with no host attached, exactly as a database connection asks by name.
Because the question is no longer "which address", the endpoint may have none: a Unix socket is
allowed, as a `unix:` URL where the setting is a URL and a bare path where it is a host. A
socket path supplied by the program is refused.
